purpose: Owner-reviewed examples that calibrate what counts as useful, out of scope, and rare-but-critical for this phase's acceptance. Bound into the adopted contract by SHA-256.

positive.example: A local user who never configures a backend upgrades Sellbird and keeps working on SQLite with the token link exactly as before.
positive.why: Upstream promise; D1 keeps SQLite as the default.

positive.example: With the Postgres backend configured, approving a drafted email in the Outbox sends it once, inside the daily limit and outside quiet hours, exactly as on SQLite.
positive.why: Sending safety is the product's core trust promise.

positive.example: Behind local Kratos and flint-gate, the operator signs in with password and second factor and reaches the dashboard; nobody else can.
positive.why: D3 operator-only sign-in; proves the hosted auth path before the platform exists.

positive.example: A merge to main produces a scanned image and a guarded digest pin for the platform overlay, with no real hostname in this public fork.
positive.why: G3/G6 restated; operator decision to keep real names in the platform repo.

rejectedOrDeferred.example: Live sign-in at the public hostname and Argo CD syncing the pod in this phase.
rejectedOrDeferred.why: Gated on the platform phase (carried goals CG-1, CG-2).

rejectedOrDeferred.example: Several people sharing one hosted Sellbird, or per-workspace row-level security.
rejectedOrDeferred.why: Multi-user excluded; single tenant with RLS deferred.

rejectedOrDeferred.example: Automated backups, high availability, Codex in the cluster, or moving the operator's real local data.

rareCritical.example: The heartbeat and the dashboard claim the same approved outbox item at the same moment on Postgres; the prospect must receive the email once.
rareCritical.why: A double send damages the sender's reputation and the prospect's trust; SQLite's writer serialisation no longer protects it.

rareCritical.example: A request reaches Sellbird with a forged x-flint-user-id header but no valid gate JWT; it must get nothing.
rareCritical.why: flint-gate forwards client headers; a trusted header without a verified token would hand over the pipeline and mailbox.

rareCritical.example: The dashboard token or the Claude credential appears in container logs collected by the cluster.
rareCritical.why: Logs are retained and widely readable; either value grants control.
